findings.reason: both sections write files §50's node also writes, and this is the same defect an earlier review raised for §55 (which was fixed by adding the edge), so without the edge a concurrent dispatch collides on `roadmap_snapshot.py` and `metadata_index.py`.
findings.text: §56 states "It runs after §50, which creates `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py`" and lists that file in its write paths, and §57 lists `reckon/metadata_index.py`, which §50 also lists, yet `plan-section-depends-on` has no `s56` and no `s57` entry, so nothing orders either node against §50 and a dispatcher can put two workers in the same files

findings.reason: the section would dispatch a worker whose declared measure passes while the duplicate cache survives behind `_parse_meta_head_shared`, and whose fence excludes the one module that must change for the deletion to be real.
findings.text: §57 lists four names to delete (`_META_BY_DIGEST`, `_META_HEAD_BY_DIGEST`, `parse_meta_shared`, `_digest_memo`) but `_parse_meta_head_shared` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:325`) is the entry point that actually calls `_digest_memo(_META_HEAD_BY_DIGEST, …)` and the only one of these with a production caller, `reckon/resources.py:284`, whose behaviour `tests/test_resource_identity_reads_the_digest_index.py:148-154` asserts; `reckon/resources.py` is not in the grep check and not in the write paths, so the node's gate can read green while a second cache stays live and the caller cannot be migrated

findings.reason: the stated reason for moving the deletion to §57 is false, and a coordinator sizing §50's fence from its write paths will hand the cache's module to a node that the text says does not touch it.
findings.text: §50 says "this section's run does not hold that module" of `reckon/metadata_index.py` and delegates the cache deletion to §57 on that basis, but §50's own write-path list includes `reckon/metadata_index.py`

findings.reason: a worker fenced to `reckon/mcp.py` and `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py` cannot return the stored snapshot when `_await_body` times out, and would either hit the fence or build a second deadline path beside the one that exists.
findings.text: §56 places the fallback "in `reckon/mcp.py`'s deadline path", but the deadline path is `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py`: the roadmap read is wrapped by `_deadline_tool(..., kind="read", …)` (`reckon/mcp.py:3319` → `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:481`), the timeout is raised in `_await_body` (`:355`), and the per-key single-recompute the deliverable asks for is the existing `_read_joining_running` (`:427`) over the `_INFLIGHT_READS` registry (`:294`); that module is absent from §56's write paths

findings.reason: the section's argument is carried entirely by where in the code each cited symbol lives, and a worker following "near line 2937" or "near line 4020" lands in unrelated code, which is exactly the class of anchor earlier reviews raised and had acted.
findings.text: after `4a54f633b` ("move the graph-target family into its own module", 2026-10-23T08:21Z) the anchors §50 cites into `reckon/roadmap.py` are stale: `_blocked_section_run_seconds` is cited "near line 2937" and is defined at `reckon/roadmap.py:2528`; `_overlapping_scope_findings` is cited "near line 4020" and is defined at `:1584`, called at `:3703`; `section_runs` "near 3083" is at `:2758`; `held_paths_by_section` "near 3100" is at `:2775`; the `in_flight` row field "near 3972" is at `:3913`; the `crew.list_live()` composition "near 3077" is at `:2752`; and outside `roadmap.py` the same drift appears — `_SERVER_CODE_STAMP` cited "near line 273" is at `reckon/mcp.py:368`, `write_plan` cited "near line 1537" is at `reckon/_store.py:1616`, and `classify_pointer` cited "near line 196" is at `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:236`

findings.reason: the section's first three cases and its negative control still fail without the fallback, so the node cannot pass on unfixed code; the pair are worth labelling as regression guards, which changes the wording rather than the work.
findings.text: §56's fourth case ("with no stored snapshot, a recompute held past the deadline reports the deadline as before") and fifth ("two reads arriving during one held recompute start one recompute") both pass unchanged on the unfixed tree, the second because `_read_joining_running` already coalesces identical reads over `_INFLIGHT_READS`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §50's line anchors into `reckon/roadmap.py`, `reckon/mcp.py`, `reckon/_store.py` and `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` no longer resolve after the graph-target refactor landed at `4a54f633b`, so several land 25 to 450 lines away from the symbol they name (plan.html:318).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §56's fourth and fifth cases ("with no stored snapshot … reports the deadline as before", "two reads arriving during one held recompute start one recompute") already hold on the unfixed tree through `_read_joining_running` (`reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:427`), so two of its five cases are regression guards rather than acceptance criteria (plan.html:342); §50's and §57's done-whens each name an explicit negative control and a wrapper-counted measure.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate writes its fragment under `docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/` (the directory exists and holds the plan's earlier fragments) and its gate logs under the run directory, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py`, `test_a_slow_roadmap_read_serves_its_last_snapshot.py` and `test_one_cache_owns_a_plan_files_parse.py` are named for what they do, with no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §57 omits `_parse_meta_head_shared`, the only entry point with a production caller, from both its four-name deletion check and its write paths, so the cache it means to delete stays live; and §50's reason for delegating that deletion ("this section's run does not hold that module") is contradicted by §50's own write paths (plan.html:318, :346).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §50 (snapshot keyed on the write generation), §56 (stale-snapshot fallback inside the deadline) and §57 (one cache owns a plan parse) each state a single deliverable with its own gate.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §56 declares in prose that "It runs after §50, which creates `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py`" and §57 shares `reckon/metadata_index.py` with §50's write paths, but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 9) carries no `s56` or `s57` (plan.html:9, :342, :346).
